insights.headline: Silver sinks to an 11-month low as gold clings to $4,000 after a bruising week
insights.summary: Spot gold hovered near $4,000 an ounce and silver near $54 after a week of heavy selling driven by crude above $116, a firm dollar and expectations that the Federal Reserve will stay restrictive. In India, silver fell to an 11-month low near ₹1.95 lakh per kg and silver funds slid, while several fund houses’ temporary halt on fresh gold ETF fund-of-fund investments remains in force. Festive buying picked up on lower prices even as gold imports slumped.
points: Spot gold traded around $3,996 and silver near $53.90 after weekly falls of over 3.5% and about 7.8%.
Silver hit an 11-month low near ₹1.95 lakh per kg in India; silver ETFs fell up to 5%.
Crude above $116 and firm US business data keep Fed-tightening bets alive, pressuring bullion.
Fresh gold ETF fund-of-fund investments stay halted at several fund houses; existing SIPs continue.
Festive demand strengthened on lower prices, but India’s gold imports slumped into the season.

trending.title: Oil, rates and the $4,000 line
trending.summary: Gold’s week was set by crude above $116, a firm dollar and sticky inflation expectations, leaving the metal fighting to hold $4,000 after dipping below it.

trending.title: Silver’s air pocket
trending.summary: Silver fell harder than gold on the week, slipping below Rs 2 lakh per kg in India, with analysts split on whether the selloff has gone too far.

trending.title: Fund curbs meet the dip
trending.summary: Fresh gold ETF fund-of-fund investments stay halted at several fund houses while silver funds slid, even as existing SIPs continue.

trending.title: Festive demand vs weak imports
trending.summary: Lower prices lifted festive buying, but India’s gold imports slumped into the season, clouding the outlook for jewellers.

trending.title: The $5,000 question for 2027
trending.summary: With gold under pressure and silver at multi-month lows, experts are split on whether either metal rebounds toward new highs next year.

items.title: Gold, silver extend weekly losses as Hormuz tensions push crude above $116
items.summary: Spot gold slipped to about $3,996 an ounce late Friday and silver to about $53.90, extending a week of heavy selling. Gold headed for a weekly fall of more than 3.5% as Middle East tensions pushed crude to multiyear highs, feeding expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep policy restrictive. Strong US business activity and rising inflation expectations added to the pressure on both metals.

items.title: Silver hits 11-month low of ₹1.95 lakh as crude stokes inflation fears
items.summary: Silver fell to an 11-month low near ₹1.95 lakh per kg in India, extending the week’s slide as surging crude revived inflation worries and kept expectations of higher-for-longer rates in play.

items.title: Bullion Cues: Bears retain control
items.summary: Gold ($3,995.80 an ounce) and silver ($53.90) fell 4.1% and 5.4% on the week, BusinessLine's research bureau notes, with MCX gold December futures down 4% to ₹1,42,024 per 10 grams and silver down 7.3% to ₹1,95,719 a kg after touching a ten-month low. Its technical read keeps the bears in control, with ₹1,41,000–₹1,40,000 the next support zone for gold.

items.title: Gold, Silver Prices Dip But Many Gold ETF FoFs Temporarily Halt Fresh Inflows: What Are Your Options?
items.summary: Gold slipped nearly Rs 1,700 to about Rs 1,44,340 per 10 grams and silver fell below Rs 2 lakh per kg ahead of Diwali and Dhanteras, pressured by Middle East tensions and US rate expectations. Since October 16, several fund houses have temporarily stopped fresh investments into gold ETF fund-of-funds, while existing SIPs continue and gold ETFs bought directly on the exchanges remain open.

items.title: Silver crashes ₹56,000/kg from August peak; gold slides ₹23,000/10 grams. What’s driving the selloff in precious metals
items.summary: Silver has crashed about ₹56,000 per kg from its August peak while gold has slid roughly ₹23,000 per 10 grams, as oil-driven inflation fears and margin-call selling deepened the precious-metals selloff.

items.title: Silver price has broken below ₹2 lakh for the first time since December 2025: Is this the right time to buy for returns?
items.summary: Silver fell to ₹1,92,800 per kg on MCX on Friday, its first close below ₹2 lakh since December 2025, after losing about ₹6,800 in a session. It is down 22.5% from its August peak of ₹2,48,800 and over 50% below January's ₹4,20,048 record. Augmont's Renisha Chainani put $50–$55 as a support zone, with a possible 10–15% rebound ahead.

items.title: Gold drops 3.28%, silver plunges 7.83% on weekly basis amid crude surge
items.summary: Gold fell 3.28% and silver 7.83% in the week ending October 24 as surging crude stoked inflation fears and hardened expectations of higher-for-longer US rates. MCX December gold closed at ₹1,42,150 per 10 grams and silver at ₹1,96,100 per kg, with gold below $4,000 for the first time since mid-July. Dussehra buying offered some support ahead of the Fed's October 27–28 meeting.

items.title: Silver ETFs fall up to 5% as oil surge, inflation fears hit bullion markets
items.summary: Silver exchange-traded funds fell up to 5% as the oil surge and inflation fears hit bullion markets, tracking the sharp slide in the underlying metal.

items.title: Comex Update: Delivery Activity Goes Deathly Quiet
items.summary: Delivery activity on Comex has gone quiet, SchiffGold's update finds: November gold open interest sits near multi-year lows, the exodus of gold from Comex vaults has paused and partly reversed, and silver notional delivery volumes are about half last October's level. The piece links the soft physical bid to gold's continued slide.

items.title: RBI’s forward dollar sales surge to record $200 billion in August
items.summary: The RBI's net forward dollar sales position climbed to a record $200.06 billion at the end of August from $136.77 billion in July, central bank bulletin data showed. The central bank also made record net spot purchases of $43.26 billion in August as it absorbed inflows from deposit schemes, balancing the flows with swaps.

items.title: Gold Tests $4,000 as India's Import Slump Clouds the Festival Outlook
items.summary: Gold settled Friday at $3,997.48 an ounce — below $4,000 at the close for the first time since mid-July — ahead of the Fed's October 27–28 meeting. India's September gold import bill collapsed to $1.8 billion from $9.61 billion a year earlier on higher duties and soft demand. Dealers report healthy festival restocking, but IBJA put Dussehra buys 7–10% below last year.

items.title: India gold demand strengthens on lower prices, festive purchases
items.summary: Gold buying picked up in India this week as lower prices during Dussehra encouraged purchases and lifted dealer premiums to up to $9 an ounce from $7 last week. Jewellers reported packed stores for the festival, though dealers said demand remained well below last year's levels. Spot gold hit its lowest since July 20 during a week set for its steepest loss since June.

items.title: Silver selloff seems overdone, says Mirae Asset Sharekhan; here's why
items.summary: Mirae Asset Sharekhan's Praveen Singh says silver's selloff looks overdone after spot broke support near $58.60 on October 14, though the crude oil/silver ratio falling through support around 58 leaves silver vulnerable to further oil gains. Registered COMEX inventory of 103.33 million ounces is down about 49% from the September 2025 peak of 201 million ounces.

items.title: Silver's Sell-Off Isn't One Story: Oil, Margin Calls and the Fed All Pulled the Trigger
items.summary: Silver's 5.6% weekly drop to $53.96 an ounce, its lowest since November, traces to three forces at once: oil-driven inflation fears, liquidity selling as tech shares fell and margin calls hit, and the Fed's October 27-28 meeting. CPM Group's Jeffrey Christian sees scope for a further slide toward $50 or $48 before any recovery, with pressure possibly lasting through the US midterm elections.

items.title: Gold edges back above $4,030 after dipping below $4,000 to a three-month low
items.summary: Gold recovered to $4,030.67 an ounce on Friday, October 23, after touching $3,986.50 — its lowest in more than three months — but remains on course for a second straight weekly loss as oil-driven inflation fears and hawkish Fed bets kept pressure on bullion. Silver slid another 1.3% to $53.81 an ounce, while platinum slipped to $1,557.03 and palladium to $1,050.50, WAM reported.

items.title: Gold drops below $4,000 as 'haven' asset joins market sell-off
items.summary: Gold fell below $4,000 an ounce on Friday, its first move beneath that level since late July, as a tech-led equity selloff forced investors to raise cash and swept even the haven asset into the retreat. Spot recovered to about $4,015 but remains on course for its weakest weekly performance since June after a near-3% Thursday slide, with money flowing into Treasuries instead of bullion.

items.title: Central banks pile into gold as China leads buying spree
items.summary: Central banks bought an estimated 79 tonnes of gold in August — nearly five times the pre-2022 average — led by China, Goldman Sachs estimates. China's purchases are put at about 25 tonnes versus an official print of roughly 20 tonnes, extending its dollar-diversification buying streak. Goldman says elevated official demand should keep gold supported over the long term.

items.title: Gold's $4,000 Looks Indefensible as Liquidation Fears Overshadow Treasury Rally
items.summary: Gold slipped below $4,000 even as the US 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.96%, breaking the usual pattern in which lower yields support bullion. ActionForex attributes the divergence to liquidity and positioning pressure, possibly including forced selling, as a tech-led equity selloff drove defensive buying of Treasuries instead. Its technical view puts next support at $3,924-$3,942.

items.title: Could silver rebound in 2027? What experts predict will happen next
items.summary: After falling from record highs above $100 an ounce earlier this year, silver is trading in the upper $50s to lower $60s, and experts cited by USA Today expect it to stay volatile in a broad $50 to $70 range into early 2027. Fed rate policy is the main near-term pressure, while industrial demand from electronics, solar panels and data centres supports the longer view.

items.title: Will gold hit $5,000 again? What experts expect for 2027
items.summary: Gold passed $5,000 an ounce for the first time early this year but has since pulled back to the low-$4,000 range, and experts cited by USA Today see a return above $5,000 as likely in 2027 rather than 2026. A strong dollar, Fed tightening expectations and soft Indian demand cap the near term, while central-bank buying supports the longer view.
